subject: LedgerScale: Private VPC fit & IP allowlist verification
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@ledgerscale.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: LedgerScale: Private VPC fit & IP allowlist verification

Thanks again for the call today, Daniel — great discussion. Quick recap + asks so we can confirm fit and scope for a Private VPC (PrivateLink) deployment versus Dedicated capacity: 

Summary from our side:
- LedgerScale prefers private connectivity for production due to regulatory requirements (you mentioned SOC 2 + contractual data residency).
- Two candidate modes: (A) PrivateLink endpoint into your VPC (recommended for tenant isolation & simpler routing), (B) VPC peering (possible but requires more cross-account routing config).

Network/ops asks (what we need from you to finalize presales design):
1) Which connectivity mode does your network/security team prefer (PrivateLink vs peering)?
2) If PrivateLink: an initial list of outbound firewall allowlist entries (we’ll provide the expected service IP set for egress and control-plane connections).
3) If peering: preferred VPC CIDR(s) and any overlapping ranges we should know about.
4) Who on your side will own the IP allowlist/portal changes? (name, email, and expected SLA window for changes)
5) Any procurement timeline constraints for Dedicated capacity if Private VPC is not required?

Next steps we propose:
- We’ll send a first-pass IP list and a simple diagram showing PrivateLink flow (attaching a quick diagram + CSV with the typical egress set).
- If useful, schedule a 30-minute network ops working session this week to confirm NAT/egress and TLS termination expectations.

Attachments planned: privatelink-ip-list.csv (sample egress/ingress CIDRs), redwood-privnet-diagram.pdf (high-level flow).

If you can reply with the answers to items 1–4 and confirm a time for the ops session, we’ll lock the recommended configuration and update the mutual action plan.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@ledgerscale.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@ledgerscale.com
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: LedgerScale: Private VPC fit & IP allowlist verification

Ben — thanks for the recap. Short answers from our side and a note from security below.

1) Preference: Security strongly prefers PrivateLink (they want no routing across accounts unless necessary).
2) PrivateLink specifics: security@ledgerscale.com will own the allowlist updates. They asked for a single CSV with the endpoints / IPs we need to add.
3) N/A for peering — we’d avoid peering unless there’s a blocker.
4) Owner: Rachel Lin, Network Ops Manager (rachel.lin@ledgerscale.com). She’s copied on the separate security thread but not on this outbound list — I’ll loop her if needed.

Notes from LedgerScale security (summarized):
- Need clarity on whether any Redwood control-plane traffic originates from third-party cloud provider addresses vs fixed static ranges.
- We require a 7x24 window for emergency allowlist changes (we can provision that on our side).

I can join a network working session Thurs (30 Sep) 10:00–11:00 PT. Let me know if that works.

—Daniel
Daniel Park
Head of Cloud Engineering
LedgerScale

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@ledgerscale.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: LedgerScale: Private VPC fit & IP allowlist verification

Thanks, Daniel — this is perfect and aligns with our recommendation. Two quick clarifications before the ops call: 

A) Control-plane vs data-plane: our control plane (account management, billing webhooks) uses a regional set of static IPs; inference egress (the tokenized model traffic) will come from a small, documented egress pool when using PrivateLink. We’re attaching the preliminary CSV and a diagram for your network team.

B) TLS termination: Redwood terminates TLS at the PrivateLink endpoint (we maintain end-to-end TLS to the service). If LedgerScale requires mutual TLS on top of the PrivateLink, we can discuss but that adds additional cert ops.

C) Emergency allowlist process: we can support a 24/7 contact routing for emergency updates — please confirm the contact and preferred escalation channel (PagerDuty, Slack, email).

Attachments:
- privatelink-ip-list.csv (sample egress + control-plane static ranges)
- redwood-privnet-diagram.pdf (PNG-style diagram embedded in PDF)

Call: Thurs 30 Sep 10:00 PT is good for us. I’ll send a calendar invite and include our network engineer (Priyom) for the technical thread.

Thanks,
Ben
<Attachment: privatelink-ip-list.csv (text/csv)>
